column1: # What the differential test compares, and where each file came from.
# Columns: role, source (commit:path, a release asset, or the path in this repo), sha256 of the bytes.
# The one published build is the rolling dev pre-release, built from 0a3073b; its installer carries the Steam
# (Mono, BepInEx 5) payload under plugins/ and the Xbox Game Pass (IL2CPP, BepInEx 6) payload under plugins-il2cpp/.
# There is no v* release and no predecessor repo. Config/WobblyLifeConfig.cs is the reader both payloads read
# the .cfg with (the IL2CPP project compiles the same file); the oracle is that file byte for byte. The frozen
# reader in src/WobblyLifeHeadTracking/Legacy is WobblyLifeConfig.cs at 5ea6775 (unchanged since the dev build),
# restructured to fill LegacyConfig and write nothing, with every core constant it read written as its value.

BepInEx 6
# BepInEx 6.0.0-be.785, unchanged since the dev build. The Game Pass first-run harness ran its BepInEx/core/BepInEx.Core.dll
# (sha256 352aacc2d5356489a00891f76db28b6463c81d25bcb02f90035171a669b7e35b) on .NET 8, with the UnityEngine.CoreModule
# of the UnityEngine.Modules 2022.3.62 package the IL2CPP plugin is built against.
# No published build shipped the plugin .cfg, in its ZIP or as a launcher-manifest.json seed (every seed is
# BepInEx/config/BepInEx.cfg), so the inputs are what each payload writes at its first start: the .cfg the dev
# pre-release's own WobblyLifeHeadTracking.dll, taken from its installer ZIP (the ZIP's SHA-256 matches the digest
# GitHub reports for the asset), writes when its WobblyLifeConfig constructor runs on a ConfigFile at a path with no
# file and the plugin's BepInPlugin metadata (v0.0.0), as the loader builds it. The Steam DLL ran on .NET Framework
# 4.8 with the Unity reference stubs of pixi run setup. The two files differ only in the "Acceptable values" comment
# lines, which list whichever KeyCode each harness loaded; no reader reads a comment line. The test reads every
# input with BepInEx 5.
